english: the commentators and others offer a reply
why: The text answers with the root-text words 'the expounders' and so on; it is not commentators who reply.
byeye_why: ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ལ་སོགས marks a quoted lemma ("the words 'the expounders' etc."); the English makes commentators the ones replying

english:
The wisdom that arises toward them
Depends entirely upon them.
why: The person in whom this understanding arises is the one who serves and relies on the parents.
byeye_why: གང་ལ "the one in whom" this understanding arises is the one who relies on them; the English makes the wisdom depend on them

english: The actions of the Supreme Sage
why: MMK 17.2 says the Supreme Sage taught that actions are intention and the intended; they are not the Sage's own actions (the genitive here stands for the agentive).
byeye_why: the e-text has the genitive གི, which the English follows; MMK 17.2 has the agentive (the Sage taught actions as…), so the doctrine supports the reviewer

english: In this context, being authentic means that non-deceptiveness remains uncontradicted.
why: The Tibetan denies the claim: the absence of anything that defeats non-deceptiveness is not genuine there (in dreams), since in a dream one later experiences that same thing or something else.
byeye_why: the Tibetan is affirmative (…རྣལ་མ་ཡིན་ནོ) and the English matches it; the reviewer read a denial into it from the dream example that follows

english: Then by abandoning it, a bad reputation arises
why: The stanza contrasts with the next (fame waxing for one who treats anger as an enemy): ill repute, waning like the dawn moon, comes to one who does not give up anger; the note rationalizes the inversion.
byeye_why: the Tibetan literally says "if there is no anger… by abandoning, ill repute arises", which the English follows with a rationalising note; the contrast with the next stanza supports the reviewer, but the line is obscure

english: they said:
why: The speaker is Moon, to whom 'the youths' reply in the next sentence; 'they' blurs who speaks.
byeye_why: the subject of མཐོང་ནས་སྨྲས་པ is Moon (the youths answer next); "they said" gives the words to the group

english: This is because all is understood through the function of the eye.
why: This is an unwanted consequence ('for then everything would be known by the operation of the eye'), and the English states it as a fact.
byeye_why: ཕྱིར་ཏེ inside a prasaṅga ("it would follow… which is not wanted"): the English can be read as the reason for the absurdity, but it reads as a plain assertion

english: to counteract the abandonment of non-virtuous phenomena that are incompatible with liberation, such as wrong views,
why: Right view etc. are cultivated as the antidote that abandons wrong views and other unwholesome dharmas, not to counteract their abandonment.
byeye_why: སྤོང་བར་བྱེད་པའི་གཉེན་པོ "the antidote that abandons" wrong views became "to counteract the abandonment of" them

english: Since it is possible for a cause to exist without the result, this also thoroughly expresses the answer
why: 'Since a cause can exist without its result' is part of the objection being answered, not the author's own reason.
byeye_why: …ཞེས་བྱ་བའི་ལན: the clause is the objection being answered; the English makes it the author's own reason

english: the Sangha monastic community must quickly offer assistance and guidance regarding punishments and the like
why: The disciple is to help the preceptor quickly receive the penance etc. from the Saṅgha and be quickly freed; the Saṅgha is not the helper.
byeye_why: དགེ་འདུན་ལས "from the Saṅgha": the disciple helps the preceptor receive the penance from the Saṅgha; the English makes the Saṅgha the helper

english: The actual engagement of the mind with an existing entity, by producing a cause characterized by a conflicting habitual tendency, causes the mind that grasps non-existence to sever the continuity.
why: It is the cognition of non-existence that cuts off the continuity of the cognition of an entity by producing a contrary cause (a vāsanā); the English makes the entity-cognition the producer.
byeye_why: the agentive བློས makes the non-entity cognition the one that cuts off the entity-cognition's continuity; the English makes the entity-cognition produce the cause

english: Even so, this does not mean the capacity is hindered.
why: The Tibetan says that case is not one of unhindered capacity, i.e. the capacity has not yet become unobstructed.
byeye_why: ཐོགས་པ་མེད་པའི་དོན་མ་ཡིན "it is not a case of UNhindered capacity" became "this does not mean the capacity is hindered"

english: what need is there for gold, jewels, pearls, or lapis lazuli to honor the Bodhisattva Mahasattva Dharmodgata?
why: The merchant's daughter offers him the gold, jewels, pearls, lapis etc. with which he is to honor Dharmodgata (abbreviated sūtra quotation); the English invents a rhetorical question dismissing them.
byeye_why: ཁྱོད་གང་གིས "the gold or jewels with which you are to honour Dharmodgata" became "what need is there for gold…": an invented dismissal

english: How can the effect be hollow just because the cause is hollow?
why: The question is how the cause (pradhāna) is also hollow because the effect is hollow; the direction of inference is inverted.
byeye_why: "how is the cause also hollow because the effect is hollow" became "how can the effect be hollow because the cause is hollow": the direction is inverted

english: It is not correct to understand that the perception is produced by [note: a single whole].
why: The rejected claim is that the cognition is produced by that conjunction, not by a single whole.
byeye_why: དེས "by that" refers to the conjunction (ལྡན་པ) of blue etc.; the note makes it "a single whole", the view the passage has just denied

english: Dawa is captivating and separated from...
why: The plotter says Candra must by some means be separated from Yid 'phrog (the domain/what he has captured), not that Candra is captivating.
byeye_why: ཡིད་འཕྲོག is a name/the thing Moon is to be parted from; the English makes Moon "captivating"

english: This means that the abbot does not only ask questions
why: The niśraya teacher too performs these services, the only difference being that he need not ask permission.
byeye_why: གནས་ཀྱིས་ཀྱང་ཞུ་བར་མི་བྱར་ཟད "the niśraya teacher also does it, only he need not ask" became "the abbot does not only ask questions"

english: Even if any particularity of wind and so forth is the cause, all particularities will not be endowed with all attachments and so forth; because at all times a definite result is seen, it is to be inferred.
why: Everything from གལ་ཏེ to ཞེས་དོགས་པ་བསུ་བ is the objection anticipated by 'However, the result...'; the English presents its first part as the author's own statement.
byeye_why: the whole of གལ་ཏེ…ཞེས་དོགས་པ་བསུ་བ is an anticipated objection; the English presents its first half as the author's statement

english: cold and the like [act upon] fire and the like
why: The example is fire etc. as the cause of diminution of cold etc. (cf. 'fire, which opposes cold' below), not cold acting on fire.
byeye_why: གྲང་བ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་མེ "fire (the counter) of cold" became "cold acts upon fire": the relation is inverted

english: that result which falls upon the head of the milkman thrown by the hand of peace
why: ཞོ་རྫིའུ is a small pot of curd, which is thrown by Śānti's/Peace's hand and lands on someone's head; it is not a milkman.
byeye_why: ཞོ་རྫིའུ is a small pot of curd, not "the milkman" (a real error; typed agent, it is a term/referent error)
